reasoning_notes.reasoning: With no history and simultaneous choices, a moderate quantity balances market price against volume. Quantity 7 earns positive profit if the other firms produce a combined amount below 17; aggressive output risks pushing price toward cost.

With no history and simultaneous choices, a low quantity limits losses if others produce heavily. Since price falls with total output and can drop below marginal cost, withholding production is a cautious opening.
With no history or known endpoint, choose a moderate quantity: this balances earning margin against lowering the shared market price and leaves room to adapt to observed choices.

With B at 0 and C at 6 last round, A's 7 earned 77. Against the same rival quantities, 6 maximizes profit: price 18, margin 12, profit 72; 7 yields 77, so 7 actually remains slightly better. Choose 7.
A produced 7 and C 6 last round, leaving B at zero. With total output 13, price was 17. Choosing 7 gives price 10 and a profit of 28, while matching 6 yields 24; more output lowers price further.

At the observed total output of 13, price was 17. Matching my previous quantity of 6 is a cautious choice: it earns 66 if rivals repeat, while avoiding an aggressive increase that could push price toward marginal cost.
A quantity of 5 is a cautious best response if rivals repeat roughly 6–7 units: it keeps total output near the profitable range while avoiding the losses that higher output could cause.

Round 1 suggests rivals may produce around 6–7 each. With their combined output near 12–13, quantity 4 keeps price near 11–12 and yields positive profit; higher output risks pushing price toward or below cost.

My quantity of 5–7 has been profitable. Given rivals’ observed quantities, 7 balances capturing output at a profitable price against the risk of market price falling if they produce more.
